persona_2.name: The Privacy Guardian
sample_responses: Thinking about my neighbor (an elderly Christian lady), I believe that she would not like this future, precisely because of the ethical dilemmas. For example, I, who am younger, can understand the benefits and risks and am willing to take them. Religions must also be taken into consideration, although I do not have one, other people do, as is the case with my neighbor, and I believe that she would not like decisions such as death to be made by artificial intelligence.

My previous discomfort with AI in other contexts—like the AI Death Doula, AI Influencers, and AI emotional companions—stems from a similar concern: I don’t want AI to dominate or depersonalize deeply human experiences. Scenario 2 keeps AI in a supportive role, handling mundane tasks while leaving room for human creativity and collaboration. This balance ensures I can maintain my independence and focus on meaningful, creative work without feeling constrained by an AI-driven corporate system.

Scenario 2 is preferable because it preserves the authenticity of human relationships and ensures that emotional connections remain meaningful and real. While emotionally attuned AI could offer support, over-reliance on AI for companionship could weaken human bonds and social skills. Maintaining AI as tools rather than emotional partners ensures that people continue to seek and value real human connections while still benefiting from AI’s practical support.
